messages:
ana: Heads up — we're seeing a gap where parent spans are missing for requests that hit the new api-gateway canary. Traces come in as lots of root spans instead of child spans. Not sure if it's propagation or exporter side. :eyes:

mike: I noticed the same on the frontend -> policy-service path. Most of the spans have a strange `traceparent` that doesn't match upstream logs.

sara: timeline: envoy canary rolled ~15:22 UTC (deploy-bot posted). After that we started seeing ~1-2% of requests with orphaned spans.

deploy-bot: canary deploy: envoy v2.14.3 -> v2.15.0 by @infra at 2025-06-02T15:22:10Z

kevin: quick sample of headers from a broken request (sanitized):
```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.dev
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
tracestate: vendor1=abcd1234
user-agent: curl/7.79.1
x-forwarded-for: 10.2.3.4
```

kevin: but when the same call gets to our ingress-router the traceparent becomes: `00-00000000000000000000000000000000-0000000000000000-00` or is missing entirely.

ana: typo — I mean ana :)

ana: (fixing) cc @infra — looks like header rewriting in the new envoy config may be dropping or normalizing `traceparent`.

mike: repro steps I'm using: curl -> envoy canary -> router -> policy-service. If I bypass envoy canary directly to router, propagation is fine.

kevin: possible causes: header canonicalization (envoy normalizers), h2->http1 conversion munging headers, or our router's header whitelist. We recently added `x-*` whitelist changes in the router config last week.

ana: also note that OTLP exporter is complaining about span parent IDs missing in logs, but the exporter itself is up. We get 202s then payloads with many parentId=null.

infra-bot: alert: increased trace parent-null rate at 2025-06-02T15:24:05Z, pattern: requests routed via envoy canary

kevin: troubleshooting I did: enabled request/response_header logging in the canary. Confirmed the `traceparent` is present on ingress side of canary, but absent on egress to our router upstream cluster. Looks like header was intentionally removed in the Envoy route config: `remove_request_headers` set.

ana: yay detective work. Who changed that route config?

mike: @tj pushed a change to the gateway last Friday that simplified header rules (PR #4572). I think it removed some `trace*` passthroughs to avoid leaking internal baggage.

tj: yep I pushed that. I intended to block `baggage` and custom vendor headers but kept `traceparent`. Looks like my regexp was too broad and matched `trace*` so it nuked `traceparent` as well. Sorry — my bad.

sara: low-effort mitigation: update envoy route to explicitly `preserve_external_request_headers: ["traceparent","tracestate"]` or remove the `remove_request_headers` entry for those keys.

kevin: Ops mitigation plan proposed: 1) rollback the canary (quick) OR 2) hotfix route config to whitelist the exact headers (less flappy). Which do we want?

ana: rollback will restore propagation immediately but loses other canary fixes. Hotfix is small and low-risk. I'm for hotfix.

tj: I'll prepare a patch to change the header removal to a safe list. Will post PR in 10m.

infra-bot: note: we have a safety net — our trace-merge job attempts to link by request_id when parent is missing, but that only helps ~30% of cases.

mike: for observability — we should backfill a dashboard metric for "traceparent-missing-rate" at the router ingress and api-gateway egress. Right now we only track spans accepted by ingest.

sara: Agreed. Adding a graphed alert threshold at 0.5% will catch future misconfig. Also add an annotation on the deploy dashboard noting the gateway change.

tj: PR: https://github.com/redwood/gateway/pull/4598 — update remove_request_headers -> explicit preserve list. Rolling out hotfix to canary cluster now.

mike: after patch applied the canary egress headers show `traceparent` preserved. Re-run trace test — child spans appear again.

ana: good verification. Let's ship canary-wide change but keep an eye for any vendor-baggage leakage. Also add unit test in infra config CI to reject patterns that remove `traceparent`/`tracestate`.

tj: will add test and a short note in the PR.

kevin: follow-ups: 1) small dashboard, 2) CI guard for header rules, 3) postmortem note in incidents if needed. Who wants action items?

sara: I'll own the dashboard + alert.

mike: I'll add CI guard in infra-config repo.

ana: I'll draft a short incident slack summary for #general and tag infra.

infra-bot: action recorded: rollback option still available until 2025-06-02T18:00:00Z; current remediation: hotfix applied to canary; monitoring to follow.

ana: thanks everyone. If anyone sees reappearance ping here. :thumbsup:
